Expected value labels from a PV

Source: R/value_labels.R
pv_value_labels.Rd

Derives from the we-tags of a PV which codes and value labels each variable should have in the field data. Grouped items (dates, multiple choice items, lists) are split into one set of codes per variable, like in pv_var_labels().

Usage

pv_value_labels(pv)

Arguments

pv

The result of read_pv(), or a path (or several paths) to PV docx files.

Value

A data frame with one row per variable and code and the columns var, code, label, list (name of a list like [Gemeindeliste] the codes come from, otherwise NA), item, va and pv. Variables of the PV without any code (e.g. open questions without buttons) have one row with code NA.

Details

The lines of a we-tag are read as follows:

  • 1: Arbeiter/in gives code 1 with the label "Arbeiter/in".

  • Conditions in front of a code are removed: if (h_etauto = 0) 5: Mitarbeiter gives code 5.

  • BUTTONS: verweigert (-97), ... gives code -97 with the label "verweigert", and so on. Conditions in the buttons ([if h_panel = 0] bis heute (-5)) are removed from the label.

  • Hints for the interviewer in << >>, OFFEN: lines and date fields (Monat ____ Jahr _____) give no codes.

  • Multiple choice items: the lines in square brackets ([0: nicht genannt], [1: genannt]) are the codes of every variable of the item. The lines for the single variables (ts23525 1: Sonderzahlungen ...) give no codes.

  • Dates: the month variable gets the codes of the buttons and the season codes from the in-tag (21=Jahresanfang/Winter, ...). The other parts of the date only get the codes of the buttons.

  • A list in square brackets (e.g. [Gemeindeliste]) means that the codes come from a list that is not in the PV. The name of the list is kept in the column list, the buttons of the item are read as usual.

  • If the same code appears several times with different texts (e.g. under different conditions), every text is accepted.

See also

value_label_test(), which uses this function. Call it yourself (nepstest:::pv_value_labels()) to see which codes a variable is expected to have.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
values <- nepstest:::pv_value_labels("NEPS_B180_SC6_EP_26ET_V2_2_20250312.docx")
values[values$var == "etbs", ]
} # }
